title: 2025 Year in Review: Self-Evolution and Life Echoes
summary: This year I made the leap from "technical executor" to "life architect."
markdown:
![image]()
> Keywords of the year: evolution, self-consistency, feet on the ground

## 📊 2025 Dashboard

**Cognitive input**
- 🎧 Podcasts: 147 days × 108 episodes = 77 hours of mental upgrade
- 🎵 Music: 5,524 songs × 509 hours, 54% new-song exploration

**Habits**
- 🏃 Pomodoro check-ins: 129 sessions = 42.5 hours of ritual
- 💤 Sleep rhythm: bed by midnight, up at 7 — all year long

**Health wins**
- 💪 Fatty liver: gone ✓
- 🧘 Steady mind: full recovery after thyroid surgery

**Tool investment**
- 🛠️ AI stack: Windsurf, Cursor, Claude, Readdy, Figma, Paraflow

**Relationship breakthroughs**
- 💑 Zero fights: 365 days of a real shift in how my wife and I talk
- 👨‍👦 Parenting growth: from mutual blame to mutual apologies

**Creative output**
- 🚀 Project Prompt launched

---

## 1. Growth: Inner and Cognitive Transformation

This year I made the leap from "technical executor" to "life architect."

- **Awakening of the year: from Xiaoyuzhou to "managing life"**
- In 2025, *Zhi Xing Xiao Jiu Guan* on Xiaoyuzhou became the lever that cracked open my "tech cocoon." It showed me that finance is not cold numbers — it is a way of looking at life. I finally got "managing money is managing life": every allocation of resources is a vote for the life I want. That cross-domain lens taught me delayed judgment, the complexity of the world, and let go of a lot of blind money anxiety. Across 147 days I listened to 108 episodes, totaling 77 hours. Those voices kept me company on commutes, walks, and chores — turning scrap time into golden hours for upgrading how I think.

- **Challenge and resilience: from coder to AI conductor**
- The AI era is both challenge and opportunity. This year I evolved from "let AI write a line" to "orchestrate AI to ship a whole project." I learned the essence of AI-assisted coding: the ability to ask beats the ability to type; architectural intuition beats memorizing syntax. Stretching that boundary gave me the confidence to solve real-life problems and build interesting products on my own. It was also the year I truly embraced the AI tool ecosystem — Windsurf, Cursor, Claude Code Max, Readdy, Figma, Paraflow, and more. Those subscriptions were not just money spent; they were a vote of confidence in the productivity tools of a new era.

- **Hardcore practice: Project Prompt is born**
- I built and shipped this product myself. The goal: turn fuzzy ideas into professional prompts so AI actually understands product logic. It is more than a tool — it was my ultimate field test as a "full-stack creator" in 2025, proof of how much force logic and tools can unleash together.

- **New discoveries about myself: "holding" emotion and "grounding" action**
- Holding my temper: with my wife and kids — the people closest to me — I learned to "make the case without losing my cool." My proudest win this year: zero fights with my wife. That is not dodging conflict; it is communicating more maturely — listen first when we disagree, cool down first when emotions rise. That gentle firmness made home more stable and moved our marriage into a new chapter.
- Feet on the ground: I gradually left pure daydreaming behind and let ideas "touch soil." I know more clearly what I actually like, and outside noise bothers me less. That steadiness is the most solid growth of the year.

- **Growing both ways with my child: parenting as self-practice**
- How I relate to my kid changed in quality this year. I started apologizing first; he learned to apologize on his own. Home is no longer a battlefield of dumping blame. My son stopped yelling and learned to reason with us. That mutual influence made me realize: parenting is not one-way instruction — it is two-way cultivation.
- What moved me more was seeing his sense of responsibility and initiative. He started learning to read; we only need to say "time for reading," and he gets to it. The unforgettable one: before the kindergarten storytelling contest, we picked *The Money King Shooting the Tide*. He went into the study alone, listening and memorizing the video section by section until he had the whole story. On stage he forgot the last line — but for days before that he kept pulling us over to listen until he could recite it word-perfect. That stubborn drive for getting it right showed me the force already living inside him.

---

## 2. Life: Concrete Everyday Poetry

Life is not only about getting somewhere — it is about feeling the road.

- **Body and mind: a reboot from the inside out**
- Health win: the happiest line on my 2025 physical exam was that fatty liver had completely disappeared. Weight did not drop much, but my belly clearly shrank a circle. Recovery after thyroid surgery, plus a shift in mindset, put me in a calmer state than I have known in years.
- Sleep discipline: still "asleep by midnight, up at 7," plus exercise every few days — a sense of control over my body is coming back.
- Habit building: I started using a Pomodoro TODO check-in, morning podcasts, and a twenty-minute walk after lunch. 129 sessions across the year, totaling 42 hours 34 minutes. Tiny rituals, but they made every day more unhurried and full.

- **Small joys: "nearby" and "loved ones" through the lens**
- Music as company: 5,524 songs, 509 hours, 54% new tracks. Music became my most loyal companion — energy on the commute, background for late work, a thinking partner on walks. That 54% new-song share means I still keep curiosity for the new and willingly leave the comfort zone for unknown melodies.
- Everyday through the camera: after getting an action camera, I fell in love with photography. My frames have no famous mountains — just the precious ordinary: my wife's smile, the kids roughhousing, the tree by our door that changes with the seasons, the park we have walked a hundred times. Photography taught me to stop and look. Beauty does not require a long trip; it is in the scenery you pass every day.
- Footprints: even knowing "beauty does not require distance," we still explored. Lishui, Nanjing, Jiaxing, Shanghai — every city kept our family's laughter and memories. Travel is not escaping the everyday; it is seeing life with new eyes, then returning to daily life with richer experience.

## 3. Unfinished Business: Regrets and Reflection

Real growth includes both what got done and what did not.

- **Reading regret**: a pile of books sits in the "want to read" folder; few ever get opened. Between "want to" and "finished" is not time — it is the will to act.
- **Guitar on hold**: the fingertip melodies I once dreamed of barely got practiced this year. The guitar leans quietly in the corner, a reminder that some loves need ongoing investment before they bloom.
- **Missing records**: too little written down about each day. Many moments feel unforgettable in the moment, then blur with time. Life needs more "freeze frames" if looking back is going to stay clear.

These regrets are not failures — they are starting points for 2026.

---

## 4. Outlook: Opening Chapter of 2026

Not only setting goals — setting a *state*.

- **Theme word for 2026: Growth (Growth & Vitality)**
- 2026 is a year to keep pushing. On the soil compacted in 2025, I want work and life to grow like plants — deep roots downward, force upward.

- **Firsts I want to try: from "shipping features" to "shipping products"**
- In 2026 I hope to truly cross from developer to product person. Whatever the project, the goal is to build, for the first real time, a user base of my own — and learn how to operate a product and create value.

- **A fragment of the ideal life:**
- On a weekend afternoon in 2026, I sit at my desk watching growing user feedback in the product admin. The action camera nearby is full of new footage of family laughter. In that moment, the satisfaction of work and the everyday warmth of life weave perfectly together.

- **A note to 2026:**
- "Keep the steadiness of feet on the ground. Enjoy the joy of continuous growth. Robin — go make the things that are actually interesting."
